task.title: Real-time Sync Execution Engine
task.description: Build the core synchronization engine that executes the field mappings configured in the UI. The engine should: (1) Poll Salesforce API for changes using change data capture or last modified timestamps with configurable polling intervals (5min, 15min, 30min, 1hr). (2) Apply field transformations defined in mappings (direct copy, string formatting, date conversions, lookup resolutions, formula calculations). (3) Validate data against destination schema rules before writing. (4) Handle bidirectional sync conflicts using configured resolution strategies (source wins, destination wins, manual review, most recent timestamp). (5) Queue failed syncs with automatic retry logic (exponential backoff, max 3 retries). (6) Create detailed sync logs with timestamps, records processed, fields updated, errors encountered, and conflict resolutions. (7) Expose REST API endpoints: POST /sync/execute (trigger manual sync), GET /sync/status/:syncId (check sync progress), GET /sync/history (retrieve past syncs with pagination). (8) Store sync state in database tables: sync_executions (id, mapping_id, status, started_at, completed_at, records_processed, errors_count), sync_logs (id, execution_id, record_id, field_name, old_value, new_value, error_message, timestamp). (9) Implement background worker process that processes sync queue and executes transformations. (10) Add sync health monitoring with alerts for repeated failures.
task.rationale: The field mapping UI creates the configuration, but without an execution engine, no actual data synchronization occurs. Users can't realize value from their mappings until data flows between systems. This is the critical backend component that makes the entire sync feature functional. It should be built immediately after the configuration UI so users can see their mappings in action and validate their configurations with real data.

issues: CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' for both style-src and script-src, completely undermining XSS protection. This is a critical security flaw that allows arbitrary script injection.
WebSocket connection (ws://localhost:8080/ws) has no authentication mechanism and uses hardcoded localhost URL. Unauthorized clients can connect and the code will fail in production.
No CSRF protection on any API calls or state-changing operations. Authentication token from localStorage is used without validation, creating session security vulnerabilities.
data.feedback: Critical fixes required: 1) Remove 'unsafe-inline' from CSP - use nonces or hashes for inline scripts/styles, move all inline JS to external files. 2) Implement WebSocket authentication by sending token in connection handshake (e.g., ws://host/ws?token=${token}) and validate server-side. Use environment-based URL configuration instead of hardcoded localhost. 3) Add CSRF token mechanism: generate token server-side, include in meta tag, send with all state-changing requests in X-CSRF-Token header. 4) Validate auth token before use: check expiration, signature, and refresh if needed. 5) Restrict CSP connect-src to specific domains instead of 'https: wss:'. 6) Add SRI integrity attributes to Google Fonts. 7) Implement proper input sanitization for all data rendered in tables, status badges, and diff views using a templating engine with auto-escaping.

issues: Critical Security: CSRF token meta tag is empty and placeholder values (PLACEHOLDER_HASH, PLACEHOLDER_SRI) remain in CSP headers - these MUST be replaced with actual values before any deployment or the security mechanisms will not function

Critical Security: Authentication token stored in localStorage and passed via WebSocket URL query string creates XSS vulnerability and exposes tokens in server logs/browser history - must use httpOnly cookies and header-based authentication instead

Critical Production Breakage: CSP configuration blocks Google Fonts CSS (font-src missing googleapis.com) and SRI integrity will fail on Google Fonts due to dynamic CSS generation - application will have broken styling and CSP violations in production
data.feedback: Your real-time sync engine has critical security vulnerabilities and deployment blockers that must be fixed immediately: (1) Replace ALL placeholder values in CSP - the 'PLACEHOLDER_HASH' and 'PLACEHOLDER_SRI' strings with actual computed hashes/integrity values or remove SRI entirely if not using it. The empty CSRF token meta tag must be populated server-side with a real token. (2) Fix the authentication flow - remove token from localStorage and WebSocket URL parameters. Instead, use httpOnly secure cookies for token storage and pass authentication via WebSocket handshake headers or implement a secure token exchange after connection. (3) Fix CSP font configuration - add 'https://fonts.googleapis.com' to font-src directive, and remove SRI integrity check from Google Fonts link since their CSS is dynamically generated. (4) Complete the truncated CSS declaration (.diff-field-value background rule). (5) Add WebSocket message validation/sanitization before JSON.parse to prevent injection attacks. (6) Implement exponential backoff in WebSocket reconnection logic. (7) Add proper error boundaries and loading states. (8) Make sidebar responsive for mobile. (9) Fix accessibility: convert nav-link divs to semantic buttons/links with proper ARIA labels and add skip-to-content link. (10) Ensure color contrast meets WCAG AA standards. This code cannot be deployed in its current state - it has both security holes and will break in production due to CSP violations.

issues: Critical XSS vulnerability: WebSocket message sanitization uses incomplete regex `data.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, '')` that can be bypassed with malformed HTML tags or JavaScript protocol handlers. Must implement proper HTML sanitization library (DOMPurify) or use textContent for DOM insertion instead of innerHTML.

Critical security: Missing CSRF token validation in apiRequest() function combined with credentials being sent. Add CSRF token to all state-changing requests and validate on backend. Also missing authentication mechanism for WebSocket connections allowing unauthorized access.

Critical memory leak: Unbounded array growth in state.conflicts.unshift() and state.syncExecutions.unshift() will cause browser crashes over time. Implement maximum array size limits (e.g., slice to 100 items) and proper cleanup strategies.
data.feedback: IMMEDIATE FIXES REQUIRED: 1. **XSS Prevention** - Replace all instances of `element.innerHTML = escapeHtml(data)` with `element.textContent = data` for user-generated content. If HTML rendering is required, integrate DOMPurify library and use: `element.innerHTML = DOMPurify.sanitize(data, {ALLOWED_TAGS: [], ALLOWED_ATTR: []})` 2. **CSRF Protection** - Add to apiRequest(): `const csrfToken = document.querySelector('meta[name="csrf-token"]').content; headers['X-CSRF-Token'] = csrfToken;` and ensure backend validates this token. 3. **Memory Management** - Add to updateConflicts(): `state.conflicts = state.conflicts.slice(0, 100);` and same for syncExecutions. Better: implement circular buffer or use Map with size tracking. 4. **WebSocket Security** - Add authentication: `const ws = new WebSocket(wsUrl + '?token=' + encodeURIComponent(authToken));` and validate on backend. 5. **CSP Hardening** - Remove 'unsafe-inline' and use nonces: Generate random nonce server-side, add to CSP header and script tags: `

data.feedback:
BLOCKING ISSUES:
1. CSRF Protection: Set actual token value in <meta name='csrf-token' content='{{ csrf_token }}'>
2. XSS Prevention: Replace onclick='${action.handler}' with addEventListener pattern using proper event delegation and sanitization
3. WebSocket Security: Move authentication token from URL to connection headers or first message payload: ws.send(JSON.stringify({type:'auth',token}))
4. CSP Hardening: Replace 'wss:' with 'wss://yourdomain.com' and 'https:' with specific API domains
5. Code Completion: Finish debounce function implementation and complete HTML closing tags for body/html
6. Complete all truncated sections including navigation menu and main content areas

MEDIUM PRIORITY:
7. Add responsive CSS with @media queries for mobile (sidebar should collapse)
8. Implement keyboard accessibility: add ESC key handler for modals and proper ARIA labels
9. Add rate limiting for WebSocket reconnection using exponential backoff
10. Remove !important flags from CSS and use proper specificity

The application has critical security vulnerabilities and is incomplete. Fix security issues and complete the code before deployment.

blocking_issues: Sidebar is fixed position with no mobile hamburger menu - will completely break mobile UX by covering content
Main content has fixed 240px left margin that doesn't adapt on mobile - content will be partially hidden
No keyboard navigation support for modals - cannot tab through form fields or close with ESC key
Modal close button has no accessible label or ARIA attributes - screen readers will announce as unlabeled button
Navigation links use <a> tags with data-view attributes but no href - breaks keyboard navigation and right-click context menu
Action menu dropdown has no keyboard accessibility - cannot open or navigate with keyboard alone
Tables have no responsive solution for mobile - horizontal overflow will require awkward scrolling on small screens
Filter inputs have no associated <label> elements - screen readers cannot identify input purposes
Configuration view SVG path is truncated in the source code - this will cause a rendering error for the configuration navigation icon
No keyboard navigation implementation between views - users cannot navigate the application using Tab/Arrow keys effectively
Modal close buttons lack proper keyboard trap - focus can escape modal when open, violating WCAG 2.1 AA
Form inputs missing required/error state ARIA attributes (aria-required, aria-invalid, aria-describedby)
No skip-to-content link for keyboard users to bypass navigation
Color contrast issues: --text-secondary (#666) on --bg-card (#FFF) is 5.74:1 - fails WCAG AA for small text (requires 7:1)
Tables missing proper ARIA labels and table headers lack scope attributes for screen readers
Incomplete code block at line ~350 (startSyncExecution function cuts off mid-condition)
